I read all 380 commits and the 127-row PR sheet. Here's what I found.

## The shape of the release

| Type | Commits | User-visible? |
|---|---:|---|
| chore (deps, lockfiles, configs) | 153 | no |
| refactor | 73 | mostly no — see caveats |
| test | 64 | no |
| ci | 33 | no |
| **fix** | **26** | **yes** |
| docs | 20 | no |
| **perf** | **10** | **yes** |
| **feat** | **1** | **yes** |

So 343 of 380 commits are noise for your readers. Real content is 37 commits, and those collapse further because the same fix landed in several modules independently — e.g. "guard the null cursor in the paginator" is four separate commits (queue, api, webhooks, db) that are one bullet to a reader.

The 16 dependency bumps are each repeated 5–12 times in the log with identical from→to versions, so there are only 16 net version changes. Nine are runtime deps (undici, fastify, pg, knex, ioredis, pino, zod, nanoid, dotenv); seven are dev-only (typescript, eslint, prettier, vitest, tsx, esbuild, husky) and don't belong in user-facing notes at all.

## What actually changed for users

**One new feature.** `feat(webhooks): retry failed deliveries with exponential backoff` (#4191, 395fb48). Note it also touched `src/core/config.js` — that almost certainly means a new config option to tune or disable it, which you'll want to name in the notes.

**Three behavior changes people will feel:**

1. **`fix(auth): return 401 for an expired token instead of 403`** (1d2bd55). This is a response-contract change. Anyone branching on 403 breaks silently. I'd put this under Breaking, not Fixed, regardless of its commit prefix.
2. **`fix(*): use the right units in the latency histogram`** (store 59402bc, core 1f2bc4e). Emitted metric values change magnitude. Dashboards and alert thresholds built on 4.1 will read wrong after upgrade. Worth calling out explicitly.
3. **`fix(db): stop logging the whole request body`** (1b55313). A privacy fix — request bodies were going to logs. Users may want to know so they can go purge old logs.

**Genuine bug fixes, deduped from 26 commits to 8 themes:**

- HTTP client leaked a timer when the socket dropped (f66d359) and didn't close the pool on shutdown (eb874a5) — both affect clean process exit.
- Paginators crashed on a null cursor (queue, api, webhooks, db).
- Empty allowlist was mishandled (store, db, jobs).
- Trailing slash was trimmed twice, mangling URLs (queue, jobs).
- Duplicate header sent on requests (core ×3, billing, http).
- Trace id was lost across a retry (api ×3) — hurts anyone correlating logs.
- Token parser error messages tightened (core, billing, queue).

**Performance** (10 commits): batched metric writes, removed a JSON round-trip on the hot path, dropped redundant clones in mappers, and `perf(api): reuse the parsed schema between requests` (9f02d92). Real, but I have no benchmark numbers here — I'd either omit these or state them qualitatively rather than invent a percentage.

## Two things I could not verify, and one gap

**The refactors may hide breaking changes.** These three patterns look internal but touch the export surface, and I can't confirm either way because the repo has only `history/` and `CHANGELOG.md` — there's no source tree to check `index.js` against:

- `refactor(api): drop the unused v1 export route` (56dc828) — removes a route. "Unused" per the author, but that's a claim about *your* callers, not your users'.
- `stop re-exporting the internal error types` — 8 commits (jobs, db ×2, core ×2, auth, billing ×2). If those types were reachable from the package entry point in 4.1, every `import { SomeError }` breaks.
- `move the config loader under src/config` — 7 commits. Breaks anyone deep-importing the old path.

Please diff the 4.1 and 4.2 public entry points before you publish. If any of those were exported, they're Breaking entries and this is a major-version conversation, not a 4.2.

**Possible Node version bump.** Four `docs: note the minimum node version` commits plus three `ci: run the suite on node 22`, but nothing touches `engines` in a way the log shows. If the floor moved, that's a Breaking entry.

**The history stops on 2026-06-17.** You're cutting tomorrow, 2026-08-29 — a ten-week gap with no commits. Either the branch has been frozen since June, or this export is stale and there's work missing. Worth confirming before you publish, since anything after 6/17 is invisible to me.

## Draft, in your house shape

Assumes the refactors turn out to be internal. If the export check says otherwise, those move up into Breaking.

```markdown
## 4.2.0 — 2026-08-29

### Breaking
- An expired token now returns 401 instead of 403. If you branch on the
  status code, update it.
- The latency histogram now reports the correct units. Dashboards and alerts
  calibrated against 4.1 will need their thresholds rescaled.

### Added
- Failed webhook deliveries are retried with exponential backoff.

### Fixed
- Request bodies are no longer written to the logs.
- The HTTP client no longer leaks a timer when the socket drops, and it now
  closes the pool on shutdown.
- Paginators no longer fail on a null cursor.
- An empty allowlist is now handled instead of erroring.
- Trailing slashes are trimmed once, not twice.
- Requests no longer carry a duplicate header.
- The trace id survives a retry.
```

Two calls for you: whether the perf work earns a mention (your three headings have no home for it — I left it out rather than bend a heading), and whether to name the new webhook config option once you've looked at what `src/core/config.js` gained. I can paste this into `CHANGELOG.md` at the placeholder if you want it in the file.
